Published November 09, 2026
Prince William has received an enthusiastic endorsement from one of the organisations hoping to win his Earthshot Prize.
Bijal Brahmbhatt, director and managing trustee of the Mahila Housing Trust, described William as a “thought leader” whose efforts are helping bring greater attention to climate solutions.
The organisation is among the finalists in the ‘Fix Our Climate’ category of this year's Earthshot Prize and is working to protect low-income women from the effects of extreme heat.
Speaking to PEOPLE, she praised the Prince's approach to environmental issues and the impact his initiative has had in bringing organisations and potential partners together.
“One of the taglines of the Earthshot Prize is urgent optimism, and you know I do believe that the urgent optimism that the prince has sort of generated is also being turned into transformative action, and within a short timeline, and that was what the world needed,” she said.
She added: “[We] must congratulate him for sort of being the thought leader in the space that we have been working in for [so] long.”
The Mahila Housing Trust has spent more than three decades working with women from low-income communities.
Brahmbhatt explained that the organisation initially focused on supporting women's economic independence and reducing poverty, before recognising how increasingly extreme temperatures were affecting their ability to earn a living.
In 2015, the team began looking more closely at the impact of climate change on the communities it supported.
Many women living in informal settlements work from home, often under tin-sheet roofs that trap heat and leave their houses even hotter than the air outside. Poor ventilation makes conditions particularly difficult, affecting both their health and their ability to work.
Brahmbhatt said the organisation found that homes could become almost 42 degrees Fahrenheit hotter than the outside temperature.
The financial consequences are equally serious. According to the director, the women supported by the charity earn an average of around $1,000 a year, yet extreme heat can cost them almost 23 per cent of their annual income.
She explained that these losses make it even harder for women to escape poverty, prompting the organisation to focus on practical ways to make their homes and livelihoods more resilient to rising temperatures.
The charity's selection as an Earthshot Prize finalist has already brought significant attention to its work, something Brahmbhatt described as “absolutely amazing”.
Brahmbhatt believes William's backing could help bring governments and private companies into the conversation, creating opportunities to expand solutions for vulnerable communities.
“The fact that [Prince William] is behind it will enable a lot more government and private sector attention to the space,” she said.
She is now looking ahead to the Earthshot Prize awards ceremony in Mumbai on November 17, where the organisation will be among those hoping to see their work recognised.
Brahmbhatt also hopes the event will encourage more Indian philanthropists to invest in environmental solutions, pointing to the country's growing reputation for innovation.

40°C heat warning: These areas face extreme temperatures
SAWS warns of temperatures reaching 40°C in two provinces. Find out which areas face the extreme heat and when conditions will change.
The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has warned residents in parts of the Northern Cape and Western Cape to prepare for very hot to extremely hot and uncomfortable conditions, with temperatures expected to reach 40°C.
The advisory is valid from 11:00 on Monday, 9 November, until 20:00 on Tuesday, 10 November.
Which areas are at risk of extreme heat?
SAWS expects daytime temperatures of between 36°C and 40°C in the Namakwa District of the Northern Cape and the interior of the Western Cape.
While these areas face extreme heat, the eastern parts of the country will remain cloudy and cool on Monday.
However, much of the country should see fine, warm to hot conditions from Tuesday through Thursday
Isolated to scattered showers and thundershowers are expected to return over the eastern interior from Friday and continue into the weekend.
Extreme heat could pose a health risk
SAWS warns that extremely high temperatures can reduce the body’s ability to cool itself through sweating.
This can lead to hyperthermia, a condition in which the body becomes dangerously hot.
Heatstroke is one of the most serious heat-related conditions and can kill without immediate medical attention.
People who spend long periods outdoors or undertake strenuous activities during the hottest part of the day should take extra care.
How to protect yourself
SAWS advises residents to:
- Drink plenty of water and take precautions against heat exposure.
- Carry an umbrella when outdoors during the hottest part of the day.
Residents should also watch for signs of heat-related illness and seek urgent medical help if someone shows symptoms of heatstroke.

Sudden Shift from Storms to Heat
Gauteng is entering a phase of extreme heat this week after enduring severe thunderstorms that recently hit the province. Emergency services had already placed Johannesburg’s seven regions on high alert, warning the public to stay away from floodwaters and hazardous roads during the violent storms. Now, the focus shifts to high temperatures as hot weather is forecast across Gauteng.
Soaring Temperatures Across the Province
Weather forecasters have predicted significant spikes in temperatures for major cities in the region. Pretoria is expected to lead with a sweltering 36°C, followed closely by Johannesburg at 34°C and Vereeniging also reaching 36°C.
While residents prepare for intense heat, meteorologists note that there is a forecasted 38% to 50% chance of showers during the week. These possible rains could offer some welcome relief and momentarily cool the province.
Safety Guidance from Health Experts
Extreme heat poses several health risks. Health professionals caution that prolonged exposure can lead to dehydration, heat exhaustion, and heatstroke. Children, the elderly, and those with pre-existing medical conditions are particularly vulnerable during such spells of unusually high temperatures.
How Residents Can Stay Safe
- Drink plenty of water throughout the day and avoid beverages like alcohol or excessive coffee that can cause dehydration.
- Limit outdoor activities during the hottest parts of the day. Seek shade and shelter whenever possible.
- Use sunscreen, sunglasses, hats, and wear light-coloured, loose-fitting clothing to protect from the sun’s harsh rays.
- Eat cold, light meals and consider avoiding spicy foods during heatwaves.
- Ventilate homes and workplaces well, and take cold showers to help manage body temperature.
Special Care for Animals
Those with pets are encouraged to ensure animals have constant access to shade and fresh water.
Weather Overview Across South Africa
It’s not just Gauteng feeling the impact of severe weather. Across the country, authorities are warning of a mix of fire danger, heat, and scattered rain. Parts of the Northern Cape and Western Cape are facing an extremely high fire risk as temperatures in these areas reach between 36°C and 40°C, especially in regions like the Namakwa District and the Western Cape interior.
In contrast, Gauteng is expected to experience partly cloudy and cool intervals. Meanwhile, isolated showers and thunderstorms are forecast for various areas in Mpumalanga, Limpopo, and KwaZulu-Natal. Most other provinces are likely to remain hot with generally fine weather conditions.

தமிழ்நாடு, புதுச்சேரி யில் அடுத்த 2 நாட்களுக்கு கனமழை எச்சரிக்கை: இந்திய வானிலை ஆய்வு மையம் தகவல்!
தமிழ்நாடு, புதுச்சேரி, காரைக்கால் மற்றும் அந்தமான் நிக்கோபார் தீவுகளில் அடுத்த இரண்டு நாட்களுக்குக் கனமழை பெய்யக்கூடும் என்று இந்திய வானிலை ஆய்வு மையம் மற்றும் சென்னை வானிலை ஆய்வு மையம் எச்சரித்துள்ளன.
நாளை தமிழ்நாடு, ஆந்திரப் பிரதேசம், கேரளா, மாஹே மற்றும் லட்சத்தீவு ஆகிய பகுதிகளில் இடி, மின்னல் மற்றும் பலத்த காற்றுடன் கூடிய மழை பெய்யக்கூடும் என எதிர்பார்க்கப்படுகிறது. மேலும், நாளை அதாவது செவ்வாய்க்கிழமையன்று ஆந்திரப் பிரதேசத்தின் தரைப் பகுதிகளில் பலத்த காற்று வீசக்கூடும் என்றும் வானிலை ஆய்வு மையம் தெரிவித்துள்ளது.
இதனிடையே, நாட்டின் தலைநகரான டெல்லி-என்சிஆர் பகுதியில் காற்றின் தரம் தொடர்ந்து 'மிகவும் மோசமான' நிலையிலேயே நீடிக்கிறது. மத்திய மாசுக்கட்டுப்பாட்டு வாரியத்தின் தரவுகளின்படி, இன்று மாலை காற்றின் தரக் குறியீடு 371 புள்ளிகளாகப் பதிவாகி ஆபத்தான நிலையில் உள்ளது குறிப்பிடத்தக்கது.
